Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your start/sit questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Friday of the NFL's regular season. 

What's the latest injury buzz as kickoff time approaches? Which player is the better bet for your flex spot? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 2 Rankings | Clay's Playbook | Cockcroft's matchup rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point game
articles.description: Adam Rank notes the historic two-game start by Josh Allen and what it may portend for the season.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 18: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point night

We had one of the highest-scoring Week 1s in NFL history last week. There was no way we could possibly top that, yeah? Well, I've got news for you, the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions accepted the challenge and put up massive numbers on Thursday night.

Josh Allen led the way with more than 40 points to get your week started. We went into the draft season saying Allen was in his own tier and he's proving it early on. Allen had over 300 total yards and five total touchdowns. Allen is the third player in NFL history with nine total touchdowns and no turnovers in his team's first two games of the season. The other two were Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Both went on to win MVP. Manning's Broncos also set the NFL record for most points in the season.

The Bills are the first team to record 35 points and more than 400 yards of offense in both of their first two games of the season since the Packers in 2020. The Bills have also scored five touchdowns in five red zone drives.

My guy Tristan H. Cockcroft pointed out during our in-game group chat that Allen broke the record for most fantasy points scored in the first two weeks of the season. Breaking the record of ... Ryan Fitzpatrick, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers version (as noted by Field Yates, who knew the answer to Tristan's trivia question).

Our group chat also had an interesting conversation about James Cook III. Is he a trade-high candidate because it's Josh Allen's offense, including goal-line carries -- or do you try to get more shares of Cook, if possible? Put me in the convo for more shares. I want as much of this Bills offense as possible. Especially if D.J. Moore is going to miss time.

Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir both had six targets. Joshua Palmer had a 43-yard TD reception on his lone target.

Dalton Kincaid had seven receptions for 95 yards and one receiving touchdown. He now has 225 receiving yards this season -- the first Bills player to do that since Stefon Diggs in 2022. Maybe those Travis Kelce comparisons Kincaid had coming into the league might finally be happening.

I thought Jared Goff's preseason ranking was way too low, with him going in the teens. He's put up huge numbers in the first two games of the season. He might have to continue this pace when you consider the condition of the Lions defense.

articles.headline: New York Knicks offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
articles.description: The Knicks snapped their 53-year title drought in 2026. What's next for the historic franchise during the 2026-27 season?
articles.body:
It had been a long 53-year drought for the New York Knicks before last season's team finally broke through and brought a title back to New York City.

The Knicks now look primed for another deep run in the playoffs after retaining all five starters from their championship squad. They did lose Mitchell Robinson to the rival Boston Celtics in free agency but added Andre Drummond to fill in the backup center role behind Karl-Anthony Towns while also keeping Jordan Clarkson, Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet and Mohamed Diawara for depth.

The Eastern Conference has become a powerhouse, but the Knicks are a big reason the power has shifted to the East. Can they become the first repeat NBA champion in eight seasons?

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Friday. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for all 30 teams.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Knicks coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance

Key additions: Andre Drummond

Key retentions: Jordan Clarkson, Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet, Mohamed Diawara

Key subtractions: Mitchell Robinson

The only question that followed the Knicks into the offseason after their dominant run to and through the NBA Finals was could this group be kept together? All the starters were locked in, but the bench unit was not, and owner James Dolan repeatedly stated he would not go into the punitive second apron. The Knicks couldn't keep valuable backup big Robinson around when Boston came with a lucrative offer (over $15 million per season), but key contributors Clarkson, Alvarado and Shamet all signed below-market deals to stay in New York and go for a repeat -- Vincent Goodwill

Zach Kram's offseason grade: B-

The Knicks' championship-winning roster remains mostly intact, and they signed Shamet and Alvarado to two of the best value contracts of the summer.

But second-apron concerns meant the champs' backup center spot declined from Robinson (with Ariel Hukporti at third string) to Andre Drummond. That downgrade could cost the Knicks a playoff game or two next spring. -- Kram

What we learned over the past few months

From Ben Golliver's offseason lessons piece: The second apron is more powerful than ever.

On paper, the Knicks are the ideal candidates to spend past the NBA's second apron. After all, the franchise was valued at nearly $10 billion in the latest Forbes rankings, and that was before it won its first championship since 1973.

With Madison Square Garden setting records for ticket prices and the Knicks spending months as the toast of the NBA's largest market, surely ownership would be willing to spend whatever it takes to keep the band together. Right?

articles.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews: 30 teams
articles.description: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
articles.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Atlantic Division

Philadelphia 76ers: Sept. 14

Key additions: F LeBron James, G Jaylen Brown, G Anfernee Simons, F Dean Wade, G Labaron Philon Jr., G Kentavious Caldwell-Pope

Key subtractions: F Paul George, C Andre Drummond, G Quentin Grimes, G Kelly Oubre Jr.

No team changed its fortunes from April to July as drastically as the 76ers. Taking advantage of Boston's desire to get out of the Jaylen Brown business enabled it to accomplish so much: getting a motivated All-Star feeling the sting of rejection following a career year, dumping George's contract and putting themselves in position to be attractive to an all-time great in James, who was looking for a new challenge. They also lessened their dependency on Joel Embiid's bothersome health as he will turn 33 during the season.

They filled in the blanks by adding Caldwell-Pope and Wade as plug-and-play wings, changing the complexion of their franchise in several swoops. If nothing else, they won the offseason. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full 76ers offseason recap/season preview

Boston Celtics: Sept. 15

Key additions: Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley

Key subtractions: Jaylen Brown, Nikola Vucevic

Key retentions: Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh, Ron Harper Jr.

Boston responded to its first early playoff exit since 2021 by boldly trading Brown to the 76ers, ending his fruitful partnership with Jayson Tatum. The move should improve the Celtics' long-term flexibility to build around Tatum, but next year's iteration will require the aging George to discover the fountain of youth. The 36-year-old forward has played in 60 games just once in the past seven seasons.

Even so, this shouldn't be viewed as a gap year. The Celtics return a cohesive nucleus, and they added Robinson's defense and rebounding to shore up a frontcourt rotation that was overwhelmed in the postseason.

If Tatum returns to superstar form in his first fully healthy season since a May 2025 Achilles injury, the Celtics will have a chance to win at least 50 games for the sixth straight year. Securing Banner 19, however, will likely require finding a superstar replacement for Brown sometime down the road. -- Ben Golliver

articles.headline: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta on Fabian Hürzeler falling out: 'That's all in the past'
articles.description: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta insisted he has buried the hatchet with Brighton manager Fabian Hürzeler on the eve of their Premier League clash.
articles.body:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta insisted he has buried the hatchet with Brighton manager Fabian Hürzeler on the eve of their Premier League clash.

Hürzeler took aim at Arteta after their last meeting -- a 1-0 win for Arsenal in March -- saying "only one team tried to play football" and accused the Gunners of "making their own rules."

But speaking ahead of their fixture at the Amex Stadium on Saturday, Arteta said: "That's all done. That's all in the past.

"I have huge respect for Fabian, and what he's done and what Brighton has done as a club.

"It's just remarkable, and tomorrow is going to be a beautiful game to watch, I'm sure."

Arsenal will head to the south coast amid an ominous start to their Premier League defence after taking four victories from four.

They booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday by beating Ipswich with Max Dowman scoring a brace in his sole appearance of the season.

The 16-year-old will be pushing for a first league outing of the campaign at Brighton, but when asked if the teenager has been "knocking on his door" to play, Arteta replied: "The best way to knock on the door is to do it on the pitch, not in the office.

"Then you just leave out the arguments. When a player delivers constantly on the pitch, every single day in training, that's the best way, that's the best signal for the manager. That's the best signal for his teammates, too.

"And what Max did the other day, alongside all the other players, as well, that haven't played many minutes this season, was really impressive."

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Change of environment can help Viktor Gyökeres - Graham Potter

- Fabian Hürzeler urges Brighton to stay humble despite impressive comeback win over Man United

An eighth consecutive win across all competitions at Brighton on Saturday would see Arsenal equal the club's 123-year record for their best start to a campaign.

"We know how complicated it is to win a football match at this level," continued Arteta. "So, to win seven, it tells a story.

"After the World Cup, there were a lot of unknowns about how the players and the team were going to react. We didn't have any time with them to work together.

"But I said from day one, the attitude and what I was seeing, I was really impressed with. Then you have to put it down to performances. We had a bit of luck as well, for sure, to win four matches. But we are here.

"We've got a really tough opponent tomorrow so we're going to have to earn the right to win the game. But certainly that will be the mindset of the players and the team."

Defensive trio Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapié are all injury doubts for Arsenal's trip to Brighton, while Jurriën Timber continues to work his way back to full fitness following a long-term groin problem.

articles.headline: Is Man City teen Samba a backup for Haaland, or new Pogba?
articles.description: Manchester City's 17-year-old Floyd Samba starred against Norwich and could be used as a backup for Erling Haaland this season, despite being a midfielder. What do you need to know about him?
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・Cの10代サンバはハーランドの控えか、それとも新たなポグバか？
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの17歳フロイド・サンバはノリッジ戦で活躍を見せ、ミッドフィルダーでありながら今季アーリング・ハーランドのバックアップとして起用される可能性がある。彼について知っておくべきこととは？
articles.body:
If Manchester City fans didn't know the name Floyd Samba before the Carabao Cup tie against Norwich City then they do now. The 17-year-old was handed his senior debut up front by manager Enzo Maresca and repaid his faith with two goals in a comprehensive 5-0 win.

His second finish was composed as it was clinical. Collecting the ball in the top left-hand corner of the Norwich penalty area, Samba whipped a low right-footed effort past Darren Grimshaw -- a former City academy graduate himself -- and into the far corner.

Samba is the son of former Premier League defender Christopher -- best known for a spell at Blackburn Rovers between 2007 and 2012 -- while Floyd's brother, Tyrone, is also part of City's academy.

Floyd has been part of City's setup since he was eight; he's already been called up by England, France and Germany for international youth football, but is yet to make a formal decision on his allegiance.

As well as making close to 350 senior club appearances, Chris Samba was capped 26 times by Congo DR after making his debut in 2004. But what can his son achieve after his impressive debut against Norwich? -- Dawson

Position

Ask Samba about his best position and he will tell you he's a box-to-box No. 8 midfielder who models his game on Paul Pogba, so he will have been as shocked as anyone to have made his senior City debut as a striker as he has not played regularly as a forward since he was in the under-10s. -- Dawson

Strengths

Samba is not a natural striker but you'd hardly have been able to tell based on his performance against Norwich. His first goal was an instinctive header that hinted at a real nose for goal, while his second was a sumptuous, curled finish that looked like it had been perfected carefully on the training pitch.

That would make sense given the 6-foot tall 17-year-old has carved out a reputation as a free-kick expert; he scored a particularly notable one against Manchester United in the FA Youth Cup final last season.

What was encouraging against Norwich was how well he performed with his back to goal as the No. 9, linking play well, combining with his midfielders and playing first-time passes to release his wingers into space. But long term, Samba will surely go on to establish himself as a central midfielder.

He models his game on Pogba, which is unsurprising given they share certain characteristics: They're both tall, technically sound midfielders who are unusually good in tight spaces for their size. That tends to be a hallmark of City academy products, with Nico O'Reilly being the latest shining example.

Maresca called up a glut of youth prospects to feature for the first team in pre-season, but only three -- Samba, Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite -- impressed enough to stick around for the 2026-27 campaign. This was Samba's first crack at making a strong impression, and he nailed it. -- Tighe

articles.body:
Real Madrid and Barcelona could make a future move for USMNT teenager Cavan Sullivan, after his move to Manchester City in 2028, while Arsenal are interested in a move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi in January. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid and Barcelona could make a future move for USMNT youngster Cavan Sullivan, 16, according to TEAMtalk. The midfielder has impressed since making his breakthrough in MLS as a 14-year-old and has cemented his place in the senior team at Philadelphia Union this season, with six goals and five assists in 23 league appearances. That form has earned him a place in Mauricio Pochettino's most-recent USMNT squad. Sullivan has already agreed to join Manchester City when he turns 18, but the report claims Spain's top two are keeping a close eye on his development and could swoop if he doesn't make the breakthrough into their first XI quickly.

- Arsenal are interested in a move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi in January once he has recovered from injury, says Football.London. Kroupi, 20, scored 13 goals in 35 games last season as the Cherries sealed European football for the first time, but the club would consider offers of over £80 million to let him go. Arsenal already have Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres up front but are looking to strengthen across their forward line after the exits of Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard.

- Bayern Munich are considering a move for Benfica center back Tomás Araújo, according to Tuttomercatoweb. Araújo, 24, is reported to be available for around €40 million but his arrival is reported to be tied to that of Kim Min-Jae and, according to Bild's Christian Falk, Bayern are planning fresh talks with the South Korea international over a new contract. The 29-year-old only has two years left on his deal, which runs until 2028, sparking the discussions about his future. The report claims that it comes as something of a surprise, as Bayern were open to an exit over the summer if the right offer arrived.

- Everton are open to accepting a loan exit for winger Tyler Dibling in the January transfer window, claims Football Insider. The 20-year-old has struggled to assert himself in David Moyes' immediate plans, having failed to make a Premier League appearance so far this season. Development is still the priority for the youngster, whose transfer from Southampton cost £40 million in 2025, and the January window offers an opportunity for Everton to strengthen an already depleted squad before letting him go.

articles.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 1.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Jump to:

Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props

Bowen's Game of the Week

Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans (-2.5, 46.5)

1 p.m. ET on CBS, Reliant Stadium, Houston

This line has fluctuated but at -2.5, I am all-in. Would I feel the same at -3? I wouldn't love it, but I'd be willing to bet Houston at home in a bounce-back game after the Week 1 loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Let's get into what to look for on both sides of the ball, and we'll finish with some props bets to play.

When Houston has the ball: Houston spent the offseason working on its run game, trading for David Montgomery and adding to the offensive front. And we saw a dedicated effort to run the football in Week 1, as Montgomery had 20 carries, with Woody Marks chipping in with nine. Now, was it super efficient? No. Montgomery averaged just 3.0 YPC, and the Texans registered a run block win rate of 74% (17th in the league). But it's clear that Houston wants the run game to be a foundational element of its offense. This can boost the passing opportunities for quarterback C.J. Stroud, who will see a Bengals defense featuring a rebuilt front anchored by defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II and an underrated secondary that can mix both zone and man looks. I would look for play-action concepts (which mirror the run game) to attack the Bengals' two-deep zone shells (in-breakers to Nico Collins, if he plays) while also scheming up some shot plays. I truly think Houston looks to control the tempo on offense in this one, but let's keep an eye on third downs because the Texans need to beat man coverage from the Bengals there.

When Cincinnati has the ball: I want to see this matchup against the Texans' defense. Though the Bengals looked flat in a Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Joe Burrow finished with 254 yards passing, and Ja'Marr Chase had two receptions for 12 yards), they create conflict because of scheme and talent. articles.headline: Unwavering confidence in Loveland, concern for Pitts and more to ponder going into Week 2
articles.description: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 2.
articles.body:
Well, that was a pretty great Week 1, yeah? Teams averaged 24.7 points per game, tying for the highest-scoring opening week since the 1970 Merger (2012). There were 11 teams that scored at least 30 points, tied for the second most in the Super Bowl era. And despite all of that, Colston Loveland didn't score a single point.

I know it's not necessarily just a Loveland problem. Kyle Pitts Sr. also didn't score a single fantasy point, but Pitts had Cooper Rush as a quarterback. Loveland had Caleb Williams, the highest-scoring fantasy quarterback in Week 1! It was something I heard about a lot on Sunday (I'm a Chicago Bears supporter, if you're unfamiliar). And I will tell you the same thing I told all my friends who texted me during that game and in the hours after -- I don't care. I know, I used a fifth- and sometimes fourth-round pick on Loveland in most of my drafts (and those drafts of mine that didn't secure Loveland landed Pitts). Still, I don't care. My favorite team scored 59 points in a game. It has been a while since Bears fans have had an offense this good.

And if you're not a Bears fan, well, sorry about that. But what does that mean for this week? I would start Loveland with the utmost confidence. Loveland was involved in the rushing attack and Ben Johnson has lived on a credo of "no block, no rock," so there is a sense that Loveland is going to be rewarded in the passing game. Plus, Minnesota Vikings DC Brian Flores blitzed heavily against the Green Bay Packers last week. A heavy blitz will open things up for both Bears tight ends (including Cole Kmet), who combined for nine targets -- and eight receptions -- in the teams' second meeting last year.

Johnson's teams have averaged 27.5 points in the six games against Flores. He also holds a 5-1 advantage.

Here are some other notes you should know heading into Week 2.

Bryce Young is my favorite quarterback to stream this week. I loved his command against the Bears last week. Remember, his team did put up 37 points. Young has won four straight starts against the Atlanta Falcons and has 10 total touchdowns in his five games against them.

Tyler Shough is a popular streamer this week. In Week 1, he was 8-for-10 passing for 219 yards on passes of 15+ air yards, the most such attempts by a New Orleans Saints QB since Drew Brees in Week 11 of 2018. But the Baltimore Ravens held Indianapolis Colts QB Daniel Jones to 1-of-4 passing for 23 yards on such attempts in Week 1. I know, it's Daniel Jones, but I have to give you the information. You make up your mind.

Jayden Daniels has five total touchdowns in three games against the Dallas Cowboys. But New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart showed him the blueprint of how to attack this Cowboys defense. But instead of dumping the ball off in the flat, I'm looking for more rushing from Daniels.

articles.headline: MLB playoffs 2026: Fatal October flaws for every contender
articles.description: Tired of seeing your favorite team go home early in the postseason? Here's one thing each current playoff team needs to address to make a deep run.
articles.body:
With the 2026 Major League Baseball playoffs just around the corner, two quotes come to mind from Billy Beane, the former major league outfielder and current Athletics front office executive.

"How can you not be romantic about baseball?" Beane's character asks in the movie "Moneyball." Maybe he had this year's American League West race in mind.

The real Billy Beane, in a despondent moment in 2002, told Michael Lewis, author of the "Moneyball" book, "My s--- doesn't work in the playoffs."

Beane's Oakland teams never did reach a World Series, which was more about the high variance of short playoff series rather than his stuff not really working, but you can apply that quote to each of this year's playoff contenders. They all have fatal flaws.

(Of course, two of them will reach the World Series anyway ... and that's the romance part.)

Let's break down what each contender's fatal flaw is and whether it will sink them in October -- or whether they can overcome it to make a deep postseason run.

NATIONAL LEAGUE

Milwaukee Brewers

Fatal flaw: Lack of power (tied for 28th in the majors in home runs)

The Brewers have clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title and eighth playoff appearance in nine seasons with what has been the best team in franchise history. Last year's squad set the franchise record with 97 wins, and this year's team should reach 100 with a well-rounded roster built around likely Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski.

How they got there is fascinating: Only the Cubs have scored more runs than Milwaukee, even though the Brewers might end up last in the majors in home runs. Only 32.6% of Milwaukee's runs have been scored via the long ball, easily the lowest percentage in the majors, where the overall average for 2026 is 40.6%. And here's the thing to worry about: Over the past 10 postseasons (leaving out 2020), the percentage of runs scored via the home run has gone up each year compared to the regular season.

This means hitting home runs is even more important in the postseason. Perfectly executed small ball can certainly play a role at times, but it's more difficult to put together sustained rallies against better pitching without mixing in some power. Over the past 10 postseasons, again excluding 2020, the playoff team with the fewest home runs in the regular season has gone 17-29 and failed to reach a World Series.

On the other hand, the team with the most home runs -- it has been the Yankees five times -- has reached only one World Series, with the Yankees losing to the Dodgers in 2024 (Los Angeles was third in home runs that season, just four behind New York). Those teams have gone 31-41, so they've played 72 postseason games compared to 46 for the teams at the bottom in home runs.

This doesn't mean you should write off the Brewers. For one thing, they have been hitting and slugging much better since June compared to the first two months:

April-May: .242/.328/.359, 0.71 home runs per game

June-September: .269/.349/.4

articles.headline: Don't be surprised if ... the Dolphins have a top-10 QB, the Vikings stick with Wentz
articles.description: Eric Karabell provides a list of what to watch for in fantasy football, so don't be surprised if any of these come true.
articles.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised! 

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... the Miami Dolphins finish with top-10 fantasy options at QB and RB

Perhaps this does not seem like the best time to recommend any Dolphins in fantasy. After all, the Dolphins were not favored to win their Week 1 matchup on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders, and they may not be favored in any games this season. Other than an awesome running back who many have faded due to his circumstances, fantasy managers didn't exactly flock to the Dolphins.

Many analysts were down on first-round pick RB De'Von Achane because of the mess around him. He was the lone Miami player rostered in more than 20% of ESPN standard leagues entering opening weekend, and he scored a disappointing 10.6 points in Week 1, seeming to prove the point that investing in him remains dangerous. Myriad anxious fantasy managers will rush to trade him this week for less value than he deserves. My take: Go get him, though within reason.

Achane averaged a poor 3.3 yards per carry against the Raiders, but he fared worse in two games last season, each in the first five weeks. We like that Achane saw five targets, catching four. That means something. Achane's seasonlong ranking fell a bit, but mainly because others (Ashton Jeanty, Kenneth Walker III) rose. Achane remains in the top 10. The Dolphins hardly had good QB play last season (mostly Tua Tagovailoa) when Achane was one of five running backs to score 20 points per game.

Meanwhile, running QB Malik Willis scored 16.7 points, a bunch coming on his 14-yard touchdown run to begin the second half. He is a legit runner. Fantasy managers underestimate the impact a running QB has. Remember, Justin Fields was fantasy's No. 6 QB in 2022. He won only three of 15 starts, threw for only 2,242 yards and 17 touchdowns and he still outscored most quarterbacks for fantasy, including Tom Brady, who threw for 4,694 yards and 25 TDs. Michael Vick's 2006 Atlanta Falcons lost more than they won despite him rushing for a then-QB record of 1,039 yards. He was the No. 2 fantasy QB that season.

The running really matters. It separates the Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen and Baltimore Ravens' Lamar Jackson into even bigger fantasy stars, and it is the reason why non-runners such as the Los Angeles Rams' Matthew Stafford, Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow and Detroit Lions' Jared Goff must really pile up the passing numbers to compete for fantasy stardom. The Philadelphia Eagles' Jalen Hurts outscored Goff despite 1,340 fewer passing yards and nine fewer passing touchdowns. The running is why. articles.headline: Witnessing Jacob Misiorowski's Cy Young-worthy season
articles.description: What's it like seeing a Cy Young favorite unleash a 105 mph fastball? We asked those around the Brewers' breakout star.
articles.body:
Jacob Misiorowski will have to wait until November to see if his first full major league season ends with a National League Cy Young Award, but the Milwaukee Brewers ace is the runaway winner when it comes to oohs and aahs drawn on the mound.

The 24-year-old has thrown 1,053 fastballs over 100 mph this season -- 582 more than anyone else in the sport. Powered by that unparalleled heat, "The Miz" leads the majors with a 1.89 ERA, 0.81 WHIP and 243 strikeouts.

What is it like watching MLB's next great flamethrower dominate the sport? Ahead of his final scheduled start of the 2026 regular season, we asked Misiorowski's teammates what stood out most about his breakout year.

'The velocity jumps out for sure'

Misiorowski joined Jordan Hicks, Aroldis Chapman and Mason Miller as the only four pitchers since pitch tracking began in 2008 to throw 500 or more pitches at 100-plus mph in a single season. But even those three fellow flamethrowers pale in comparison to Miz's total number of triple-digit pitches. Hicks is second on the list with 659 pitches at 100 mph in 2018, but he, Chapman and Miller were able to air it out in short relief stints while Miziorowski has done it in a starting role.

Infielder David Hamilton: "A starter throwing that hard for that long is incredible. I sneak a peek at the board. The velocity jumps out for sure."

Catcher William Contreras: "For some people, watching him pitch that fast is out of this world. Now that I've gone the whole year catching Miz, it's gotten normal for me."

Reliever Chad Patrick: "I got to see him pitch in 2024. He was bringing it then. You start to question when he's throwing 99. Is something wrong? But nothing is wrong. He's doing his thing."

Starter Brandon Woodruff: "I would reference [Jacob] deGrom because he's the closest thing to what he's doing. He's throwing fastballs to one spot, and you see how successful he is. You can do that. Just get it over the plate and you can expand from there."

Outfielder Jackson Chourio: "I start a game thinking I have to be active out there -- but no, you don't."

Outfielder Christian Yelich: "Often they know it's coming. Sometimes they get to it. Most of the time they don't."

'Like a flash'

One pitch stands out from the rest of Miz's blazing heaters this season: A 105.5 mph laser to Chicago Cubs NL MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong on June 26. It's the fastest pitch thrown this year in MLB -- and the fastest ever by a starting pitcher. 

Contreras: "That pitch was like a flash. I'm thankful for him being on my team and not another."

Outfielder Garrett Mitchell: "It was electric. Every time he throws, we're expecting something great like that. I looked up [at another pitch] and saw 104. I was like, 'Man, this guy is throwing fuel up there.'"

Woodruff: "It's hard to hit 95, so 105 is really hard. I remember when I was hitting. No thank you."

Hamilton: "I don't know how [Crow-Armstrong] fouled that pitch off. That's the most impressive thing about it."

articles.headline: Alexander Isak 'never' regretted Liverpool move even amid 'tough' injury
articles.description: Alexander Isak has said he didn't regret his move from Newcastle United to Liverpool at any point of a tumultuous first season with the club.
articles.headlineJa: アレクサンダー・イサク、「苦しい」怪我の最中でもリヴァプール移籍を「一度も」後悔しなかったと語る
articles.descriptionJa: アレクサンダー・イサクは、波乱に満ちたクラブでの最初のシーズンにおいて、ニューカッスル・ユナイテッドからリヴァプールへの移籍を一度も後悔しなかったと述べた。
articles.body:
Alexander Isak has said he didn't regret his move from Newcastle United to Liverpool at any point of a tumultuous first season with the club.

Isak's deadline day switch to Anfield last year was for a British record £125 million ($167m) but he managed just three Premier League goals, while a broken leg ruled him out of much of the campaign.

After featuring for Sweden at the World Cup, Isak has already equalled last season's goal tally in the first four matches of the 2026-27 Premier League.

Asked by the BBC if he ever regretted moving to Liverpool, Isak said: "No, never. I would never think like that."

He insisted that the leg break which cost him much of his first season wearing red was "tough."

Isak added: "Anyone who had a long injury would know. But on the other hand, when you're in a good place and when you feel good, you don't really tend to look back because it doesn't really benefit you.

"So I'm just looking forward and feel really optimistic and excited about the season, and what it can bring to us."

Isak is seeking to return to the form which saw him score 23 goals in the 2023-24 Premier League season for Newcastle.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool targeting former Bayern Munich midfielder

- Liverpool's Dominik Szoboszlai on his best position: 'I just want to be on the pitch'

"Everyone knows that success for this club is winning trophies," Isak said.

"I want to score every game. Everyone is different. Some like to set targets and some don't. I'm the one that doesn't."

Liverpool, now under Andoni Iraola's management, have drawn three and won one of their opening four league fixtures. They travel to Iraola's former club Bournemouth this weekend.

articles.headline: Why Man United's wantaway 15-year-old wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated
articles.description: Manchester United's 15-year-old wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, caused a storm this week by requesting to leave the club. What makes him so good?
articles.headlineJa: 退団を望むマンチェスター・Uの15歳神童、JJ・ガブリエルが高く評価される理由
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの15歳の神童、JJ・ガブリエルが今週、退団を希望したことで大きな話題を呼んだ。彼の何がそこまで素晴らしいのか？
articles.body:
Gabriel is another in the long line of Premier League academy prodigies who attract massive media attention before even making their first-team debut. The 15-year-old Manchester United attacker scored 23 goals in 23 appearances in the U18 Premier League in 2025-26, despite playing well above his age group, and was also named United's Young Player of the Year.

His outstanding displays have carried over to this season and, having already featured for the senior side in preseason, Gabriel marked his UEFA Youth League debut with a hat trick in United's 5-0 win over Sabah last week.

However, the talk around him suddenly moved away from the pitch last week, as sources told ESPN that Gabriel has asked to leave and requested his registration be cancelled before he becomes eligible for a scholarship contract when he turns 16 on Oct. 6.

United boss Michael Carrick had been preparing to include him in the Carabao Cup squad against Brighton & Hove Albion earlier this week before the situation took a swift turn, but ESPN sources said that Real Madrid, Barcelona, Manchester City and Chelsea are among the other top clubs interested.

So what is there to know about a player who has yet to make a competitive first-team appearance, and why is he so highly rated?

Position

As with most prodigious talents under the age of 16, it is easier to judge the player Gabriel is now, rather than predict where he will eventually settle at senior level.

Having played slightly deeper in his earlier years, he has prospered in a more advanced role, either starting on the right wing before moving inside, or operating with liberty as a No. 10 behind a central striker. In the right system, and with appropriate structural protection around him, he could also make a difference as a false nine striker.

The key is getting Gabriel into high-xG areas as frequently as possible. While he is capable of receiving the ball between the lines and pushing up the pitch via his dribbling skills, his main weapons are his excellent shooting and finishing. Therefore, a role that sees him play at the heart of an attack would bring out his most outstanding qualities.

Strengths

Gabriel excels in many of the same areas that make modern elite young talents stand out. The basic technical ingredients are all there: his close control is immaculate, he is predominantly right footed but is excellent with either foot, and his sharpness in congested areas often sees him escape situations that initially look like blind alleys. He also manipulates and protects the ball superbly.

Certain characteristics do distinguish him from his peers, though. The most pertinent being his exceptional balance and command of his body.

articles.headline: As San Siro turns 100, AC Milan and Inter prepare to build a new home
articles.description: After 100 magical years, San Siro is running out of time as longtime Serie A rivals AC Milan and Inter Milan are building a state-of-the-art new stadium. Enjoy the magical place while you can.
articles.headlineJa: サン・シーロが100周年を迎える中、ACミランとインテルが新たな本拠地の建設を準備
articles.descriptionJa: 夢のような100年間を経て、サン・シーロの残された時間は少なくなっている。セリエAの長年のライバルであるACミランとインテル・ミランが最新鋭の新スタジアムを建設中だ。今のうちにこの特別な場所を楽しもう。
articles.body:
After his 663rd and last match for his beloved AC Milan, Alessandro Costacurta had a final wish. He wanted one more kick around in his second home: the San Siro.

Only his defensive teammates Paolo Maldini (902) and Franco Baresi (719) have played more matches for the Rossoneri. Costacurta won 24 trophies in his 22 seasons there from 1986 to 2007, securing his place among the club's immortals. Towards the end of his career when it came time to renew his contract, the center back used to hand the board a signed blank sheet of paper. They could put in any number they wished and he'd continue playing.

"I never really thought that the money was the most important thing," Costacurta tells ESPN. "I was happy on the pitch, I wasn't ready for a change, I'd earned good money, and this was about continuing to play for my club at San Siro."

As he hung up his boots, he wanted to share the experience with his friends.

"I asked to have the stadium to myself," Costacurta says. "I invited a group of friends that had never played at San Siro, and I'm talking about my butcher, someone from the bank. We played 11 against 11; white jersey vs. red-and-black jersey, with no fans in the stands. It was a dream come true for them, and for me, to show them San Siro."

This weekend, San Siro celebrates its 100th birthday; it will be packed with nostalgia both for the celebrations on Sept. 19, and AC Milan's match with Lecce on Sept. 20. But it's an endangered stadium. The ground still stands beautifully tall complete with its famous spiral columns and red lattice, but before the end of the year, the facade for AC Milan and Internazionale's new home will be unveiled.

- Connelly: Soccer's 30 hottest clubs right now

- Furious fans, peeved parents and side gigs: Why does anyone want to be a ref?

- Premier League overreactions: Title race down to two teams?

Back in 2023, ESPN covered the various issues around the Milan stadium -- it was no longer fit for purpose, and AC and Inter were missing out on valuable income. It's been a polarizing debate. Some believe the beautiful stadium should be held in the same regard as the "Duomo, the Scala or Leonard's Last Supper," as Luigi Corbani, the former deputy mayor of Milan and president of Comitato Si Meazza, told ESPN in 2023.

Regardless, AC and Inter knew they could no longer stay at San Siro in its current state. They had four options: bulldoze it and build a new stadium on the same plot; renovate it; build a new stadium adjacent to the old one and then knock it down; or eke out a few more years while looking for an alternative location. After much debate and bureaucracy, they went for option C.

"It's helical ramps and vertical towers are a manifesto of Milanese architecture," Corbani says. "Why demolish a historic stadium that works well and has always been sold out since the beginning of the season?"

Enjoy San Siro while you can; it won't be around for much longer.

articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including DeMar DeRozan signing with the Nuggets.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NBAフリーエージェンシー：オフシーズンの契約・延長の評価
articles.descriptionJa: デマー・デローザンのナゲッツ移籍をはじめ、注目される大型フリーエージェント契約や契約延長を評価・採点します。
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 17: Bey signs extension with Pelicans

Saddiq Bey terms: Three years, $55.5 million

Grade: B

Bey arrived in New Orleans as an afterthought. The former Detroit Piston, Atlanta Hawk and Washington Wizard missed the 2024-25 season because of a torn ACL before shipping to New Orleans in the Jordan Poole-CJ McCollum swap.

Bey responded to his new circumstances with the best season of his career. He started 64 games (out of 72 total played) last season and averaged a career-high 17.7 points. He made 37% of his 3s and showed improvement as a perimeter defender.

So the Pelicans gave him a big raise, from $6.6 million in this upcoming season to an average of $18.5 million over the following three years, which will keep Bey in New Orleans through his age-30 season. That's a solid contract for a solid player.

It's a bit less clear how New Orleans plans to structure its wing rotation in the short and long term, with Bey, Bennedict Mathurin, Trey Murphy III and Herbert Jones all worthy of playing time, to say nothing of Zion Williamson and/or Derik Queen grabbing minutes at power forward.

To that end, it's possible that Bey's new contract could make New Orleans more amenable to a trade of Murphy or Jones, two more established wings who could fetch draft picks from contenders.

Sept 3: Rockets, Amen Thompson agree to five-year deal

Amen Thompson terms:  Five years, $208 million

Grade: A-

Thompson is the second member of the 2023 draft class to sign a rookie extension this summer, following in the steps of No. 1 pick Victor Wembanyama. That order tracks, as Thompson is the second-best player from that draft class after Wembanyama.

He might not have exploded into superstardom as some expected -- and as Wembanyama did -- last season, but Thompson still fits the profile of a future two-way star. He's only 23 years old, he's one of the NBA's fiercest perimeter defenders and he boosted both his points (18.3 per game) and assists (5.3 per game) last season while leading the NBA in minutes played.

Thompson's 3-point shot remains a glaring hole in his game, as he's at just 22% from distance in his career on low volume. That weakness could limit his ultimate upside, as he might be best suited as an ace defender

articles.headline: Pelicans, Saddiq Bey agree on 3-year, $55.5M contract extension
articles.description: The New Orleans Pelicans and forward Saddiq Bey have agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension, his agents tell ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ペリカンズとサディック・ベイが3年5,550万ドルの契約延長に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ニューオーリンズ・ペリカンズとフォワードのサディック・ベイが3年5,550万ドルの契約延長に合意したと、彼の代理人がESPNに明かした。
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans forward Saddiq Bey has agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, a deal that also includes a trade kicker, his agents James Dunleavy and Jordan Gertler of Excel Sports Management tell ESPN.

Bey missed the 2024-25 season after sustaining a torn ACL while with the Atlanta Hawks but had a resurgent first full season back last year with New Orleans, averaging a career-high 17.7 points per game. He is now locked into a fully guaranteed deal through 2029-30 with the Pelicans.

Bey appeared in 72 games for the Pelicans last season, including 64 starts. On top of his career-best scoring average, Bey also averaged 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game.

Last season, Bey recorded three of the four highest-scoring games of his career during his bounce-back year with the Pelicans -- a 42-point effort against the Utah Jazz on Feb. 26, a 36-point outing against the Memphis Grizzlies on Jan. 23 and a 34-point night Jan. 31 against the Philadelphia 76ers.

He also averaged 20 points per game and shot 40% from the 3-point line after last season's All-Star break, according to ESPN Research, while also averaging career highs in both 2-point baskets attempted/made as well as free throws attempted/made each game. 

Bey was originally drafted by the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the 2020 NBA draft. 

In 364 career games with the Pistons, Hawks and Pelicans, Bey holds career averages of 14.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and two assists per game.

The Pelicans tip off their preseason schedule against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 6 and host the Indiana Pacers on Oct. 21 to open the regular season.

NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension

New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Kings remain interested in Duren

The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.

The Pistons declined any legitimate conversation about a Duren sign-and-trade to the Kings for starting center Domantas Sabonis and have maintained a strong stance about their intention to keep Duren.

As ESPN reported earlier this month, the Pistons have a five-year offer in the $35 million per year range on the table, but that hasn't been enough to entice the disgruntled Duren to sign.

His greatest piece of leverage is a risky one -- the $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer, when Sacramento will have flexibility for the first time in Perry's tenure as general manager. Zach LaVine's $48.9 million contract and De'Andre Hunter's $24.9 million contract both expire, allowing the Kings to generate a max offer for Duren, should he be available.

But that would only be the case if Duren is willing to take a massive one-year paycut and accept the risk of the qualifying offer. Until then, the Kings remain in the background as an interested long-term suitor helping Duren's leverage. -- Anthony Slater
